results.title: Stable on paper. What about your pocket?
results.content: Dr Mahamudu Bawumia and Hon.Kojo Oppong Nkrumah have raised critical questions about Ghana’s economy. However, the Government is confident in its recovery from the cost-of-living crisis whilst forging a new economic policy initiative worth US$10bn over five years (about GH¢23bn a year). Ghanaians must understand the context when looking at the macroeconomic indicators. Be well informed about the political equalisation in these conversations and ask the critical questions about the outcome, which, ultimately, is: JOBS, GROWTH, UNEMPLOYMENT. This article does exactly 3 things: Peg the macroeconomic data side by side with the statements made Examine the prospects of the Government’s New baby “New Economy” And most importantly, whether the policies and promised 24hr economy have achieved the intended purpose of reducing the unemployment rate And finally, what the state of unemployment looks

results.title: From stability to transformation: 5 tests for Ghana’s 2027 Budget
results.content: The government proposes lowering the primary surplus on a commitment basis from 1.5% to 0.5% of GDP from 2027. A primary surplus is the excess of revenue over spending before interest payments. Reducing it leaves more room for expenditure, but also means a smaller contribution towards containing debt, other things being equal.

results.title: GAYO partners with MMDAs and schools to promote waste segregation in Greater Accra
results.content: The Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO) has partnered with metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies and schools across Greater Accra to promote waste segregation among students. The initiative, under GAYO’s Zero Waste portfolio, covers schools in seven municipalities, including La Dade Kotopon, Ledzokuku, Accra Metropolitan and Ablekuma West. It aims to help schools separate their waste at source, turn organic waste into compost, and recycle plastics. Betty Agyei, Operations and Programs Director at GAYO, said the initiative comes ahead of a government directive requiring all households to start separating their waste from next year. “When is the important time to support with infrastructure, to support this kind of policy?” she said. “It’s very important to catch them young.”

results.title: GAYO, some Accra schools turn to composting and recycling to beat the waste problem with fresh bins
results.content: Schools in Accra that separate their waste say their efforts are being wasted because collection trucks mix the sorted rubbish back together when they pick it up. Education officials in the La Dade Kotopon Municipality say the problem has led many schools to give up sorting altogether. Now, the Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO) wants to change that. Under its Zero Waste initiative, it plans to collect separated organic and plastic waste directly from schools in seven municipalities across Greater Accra. Madam Habiba Kotomah, Education Director for the La Dade Kotopon Municipality, said some schools were part of an earlier pilot that provided bins for sorting, but the effort collapsed at the point of collection. “We do the sorting in the schools. results.title: Why Financing Government is more rewarding in Africa than financing enterprise and the threat to economic integration
results.content: The gradual implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area has brought greater focus on the advantages of significantly increasing intra-African trade from the current 16%–17%. It is recognised that Africa’s economic integration will make it more rewarding to produce, invest and trade, boosting growth, jobs and shared prosperity across Africa and her 1.5 billion-strong population. The campaign now, and rightly so, is about getting African governments to enable two low-hanging key drivers of intra-African trade: visa-free travel and connected payment systems that allow Africans to move freely, buy and sell across borders using simply their mobile money wallets. This is because, according to the research desk of the Africa Prosperity Network (APN), these two moves alone can increase intra-African trade to more than 25% within the first five years of implementation.

results.title: Video captures teachers stepping on a student’s head in violent Techiman SHS incident
results.content: A disturbing video circulating on social media has revealed a violent incident at Techiman Senior High School (SHS) in the Bono East Region, showing two teachers assaulting a final-year student. The video footage, which has sparked outrage, shows the two men assaulting the student, including stepping on the student's head. The teachers involved have been identified as Mr Jerry Jones Owusu Bekoe and Mr Adusa Ameyaw.

results.title: GES investigates alleged assault on student by two Techiman SHS teachers
results.content: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has launched an investigation into a video circulating on social media that appears to show two teachers of Techiman Senior High School (SHS) assaulting a student. In a press release issued on Saturday, October 31, 2026, the Service identified the teachers as Mr Jerry Jones Owusu Bekoe and Mr Adusa Ameyaw. The statement, signed by the Head of Public Relations, Daniel Fenyi, said the school's disciplinary committee had held an initial hearing into the incident. "The committee's findings are expected to be submitted to Management through the Regional Directorate in the coming days to inform further action and decisions," the GES said.

results.title: Gov’t to fund travel costs for mother of slain teenager to attend son’s funeral in New York
results.content: The Government of Ghana will cover the full travel costs of Madam Doris Adu Gyamfi, the mother of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, to enable her to travel to New York to pay her final respects to her son. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced the decision in a post on X on Saturday, October 31, 2026, following the intervention of New York City Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani and US President Donald Trump in securing a visa for the bereaved mother. Mr Ablakwa welcomed the intervention, saying Ghana appreciated the efforts of the two leaders. "This is most appreciated @NYCMayor. The Government of Ghana welcomes your intervention and President Trump's timely decision. We have always known we can count on our own Kwame Mamdani," he wrote.

results.title: New York City Mayor Mamdani secures Trump’s approval for visa for mother of slain Ghanaian teenager in Bronx
results.content: The mother of 15-year-old Ghanaian student Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot while walking to school in New York, will be granted a visa to travel to the United States following an intervention by President Donald Trump, New York City Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani has announced. Mr Mamdani disclosed the development in a post on X on Saturday, October 31, 2026, after a telephone conversation with President Trump. He said the arrangement would allow the bereaved mother, who is in Ghana, to travel to New York and say goodbye to her son in person. “The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away. Javits Frimpong’s mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately.
